answer: An identity tends one garden of delayed-reveal work buds, grown inside a single hardware-bound forge whose sealed chamber has a unique mass signature and can advance only one monotonic counter per interval. Peers unseal a random bud and demand a live recast, checking the counter gap and heat curve. A hollow chamber copied from someone else's forge cannot match that mass-dependent curve while advancing a second counter; colliding recasts fuse the seats and slash the extra bond. Another identity therefore costs another exclusive forge plus continuous firing time, which clones cannot amortize.
